chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibrahim ibn Shayba, who said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asking him about completing the prayer in the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina). He wrote to me: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) loved increasing prayer in the two Sanctuaries, so increase [your prayer] in them and complete [it].'

key_terms.إِتْمَامِ الصَّلَاةِ: Completing the prayer (praying four rak'ahs instead of two)
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Sanctuaries (referring to Masjid al-Haram in Mecca and Masjid al-Nabawi in Medina)

ai.seo_question: Should Muslims shorten their prayers when visiting Mecca and Medina?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar highlights the specific juristic preference for offering full four-rak'ah prayers rather than the shortened two-rak'ah form within the boundaries of the two holy sanctuaries (Haramayn). It grounds this ruling in the Prophetic tradition of increasing voluntary worship in these sacred spaces, reflecting the Shia emphasis on emulating the Prophet's specific practices in Mecca and Medina.
